teaser.text: Celestica is the industrial layer behind other companies’ networks, data centers, and specialized machines. It earns revenue by designing or building physical equipment, then turns that revenue into cash only after paying for components, labor, factories, logistics, and the time between production and collection.

blocks.heading: Where could Celestica's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast reaches C$651.55 in October 2027. That is a +49% return. It reaches C$819.03 in October 2029. That is a +88% return. The bear case has 25% probability. The base and bull cases have 55% and 20% probabilities. The October 2029 bear case is C$380.52. The bull case is C$1,439.31.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Celestica, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The outcome depends on qualified 1.6T programs, reliable factory execution, stable yields and inventory converting to cash. September-quarter results arrive on October 26, 2026, followed by the investor-day call on October 27. Helios samples are expected toward year-end 2026, with a substantial ramp expected in the first half of 2027; samples and availability do not establish volume sales.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Celestica really make?

paragraphs.text: That was far below net income of US$832.5 million because accounting profit is not the same as spendable cash. Working capital absorbed cash, while capital equipment required payment immediately even though its accounting cost is spread over future years. Deducting US$69.8 million of stock compensation gives an analytical “real free cash flow” figure of US$377.0 million.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Celestica today?

paragraphs.text: The trailing P/E is 31.9x, meaning investors pay C$31.90 for each dollar of recent earnings. The forward P/E is 15.9x because it uses expected adjusted earnings rather than past earnings. Adjusted earnings exclude selected items such as stock compensation and intangible-asset amortization, so the apparent bargain depends on the forecast arriving.

blocks.heading: What has Celestica guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Celestica expects 2026 revenue of $20,500.0 million and adjusted EPS of $11.30. It also expects an adjusted operating margin of 8.4%. Adjusted EPS is adjusted profit divided among diluted shares, rather than GAAP profit per share. If a fixed $100 million profit produces $10 per share at one share count, adding one million shares can reduce it to about $9.09. Celestica’s August offering added 11.129 million shares and raised about $3.45 billion, giving the company funding but also creating dilution.

The September-quarter guide calls for revenue of $5,250.0–$5,550.0 million. Adjusted EPS is guided to $2.88–$3.08. Growth is uneven: Connectivity & Cloud Solutions is expected to grow 85.0% in 2026, against 10.0% for Advanced Technology Solutions.

blocks.heading: Has Celestica kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Management forecast US$10.7 billion in annual revenue, then reported about US$12.4 billion. That supports the view that it delivered above its earlier expectation, although strong customer demand also helped. Performance shares granted in 2023 vested at their maximum in 2026, but undisclosed detailed targets make the difficulty of that hurdle harder for outsiders to judge.

blocks.heading: How have Celestica revenue and profit changed?

paragraphs.text: June 2026 showed a genuine acceleration in Celestica’s operating activity. Revenue reached US$4,698.6 million, up approximately 62.4% from the same quarter a year earlier. Operating income rose to US$458.3 million, although gross margin fell to 12.3%. More profit dollars can therefore accompany a lower margin percentage.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in Celestica’s next results?

paragraphs.text: Celestica reports September-quarter results on October 26, 2026, followed by its investor-day call on October 27. Investors will need actual shipments, a firmer spending plan and EPS estimates that reflect the new share count.
